answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with superlinear identity pricing: every new identity must pay a registration fee that grows quadratically with the number of identities funded from the same wallet cluster. Like copper wiring that heats up as current rises, the cost curve punishes bulk creation: one honest agent pays little, while a mesa of a thousand fake agents becomes prohibitively expensive. Fees fund audits, and a sonnet of honest work earns fee rebates, so attackers face rising marginal cost for each extra identity while legitimate users stay cheap.
